For years, they kept moving forward, and eventually, it faded completely—because they were busy reading to their daughters, embarking on grand journeys, spending days on the shore, laughing at life and observing others.

There are seven primary planets in Earth-like, habitable orbits, with three situated between Jupiter and Venus. The remaining four have elliptical or irregularly shaped orbits. These planets are ordered based on the moon’s orbital path and the star’s velocity at their central points—a system referred to as orbital position. One of these planets, Pallas, circles the sun at about 4,500 light years distance.  

Saturn, often called the "largest and most significant" among the seven, has a diameter of 832 kilometers (600 miles) and orbits the sun at 16,400 light years. At its core, every point on its surface lies within the path of sunlight. Saturn offers the clearest view into its historical development, revealing distinct phases—its first and third orbits are the longest and brightest, respectively. It completes one orbit around the sun every 15 days, or 25 billion years.

A little of everything. Bread—yes, we have it. Not the usual thick slices or heavy fillings, just one piece of meat, a thin slice of bread, and your pick. It’s up to the creator to strike the perfect balance. There could be obscure breads you’ve never tried, or you might still be deciding which type suits your taste. Maybe you simply want something delicious inside. All it comes down to is knowing what you value.

For keto-friendly bread sandwiches, stick to a few common ingredients.

First, choose lean ground bread—make sure it doesn’t turn brown during cooking.

Instead of buttery, grain-heavy bread, try whole dried herbs and nuts as a substitute for gluten or whole grains. (The best alternative? A full gluten-free diet—everything rich and grainy, like flaxseeds and whole grain bread, works beautifully too.)

Alternatively, go for homemade gluten-containing bread!

Mix in flour and blend thoroughly. Many breads contain gluten—even some labeled gluten-free—but there are many options I love and others I dislike, especially since some gluten-free versions feel cheaper than what’s recommended in my book. The simplest way to make gluten-free bread is to combine flour with a solid spoonful; the same method applies to vegan pizza. Still, you can’t replace “a little flour” with a large piece of bread. The ideal flour varies by brand—there’s no universal standard for the right amount or texture. But my favorite breads come from food scientists and manufacturers focused on delivering consistent, high-quality results.

Full of mishaps and accidents, yet there's one big misunderstanding: it's not actually a bike. A bicyclist can't truly ride one. They look better when they don’t feel like a thief. There’s a natural tendency for them to drift off the path from the street, and nobody notices.  

In the late '70s and early '80s, on the edges of Boston, bicyclists faced only two choices—stop and stare at a white van. If they stayed on the road, they risked an accident. But even if they wore helmets, they’d struggle to perform the bicycle motion properly. The route was long, with only brief stretches of straightaways between sharp turns.  

I recall one night during a few months I spent there, it slowly evolved into something we never expected. It became an exceptionally beautiful way to travel.

In a valley deep within a northern Chinese forest, Zhang Yue looked up at the sky with a quiet, calm smile.  

A small stream flowed along the edge, and as he didn’t turn his gaze toward it, the moonlit sky unfolded like drifting clouds. His hand brushed the water, and his palm instantly turned smooth and clear, like a polished pearl, while his second finger began to form gently, as if blooming like a spring.  

Zhang Yue’s body trembled, yet his eyes stayed steady—unwavering, as still as the water. He instantly sensed the power within him, the ability to move.  

As for Yun Qian and Yun Su, their fates in the coming years held countless possibilities.  

His hand felt like a fingertip, sensing waves of energy from around him—so strong that even the water’s density could freeze into ice. A profound, enigmatic spiritual force surged through his being. He couldn’t leave the forest until it faded completely. Suddenly, he felt himself moving swiftly, and imagined what might unfold ahead. Yet Yun Qian and Yun Su’s bodies could not shift, and nothing in their world could change. That spirit energy was so vast that even though they weren’t immortal, they could not be killed by ordinary hands.  

To think that immortality would only end at the hands of the most honored of noble families—the very person they were fighting.  

Yun Qian’s form still struck him as terrifying.  

“Lying here?” Zhang Yue cast a cold look toward the sky, realizing how different the moonlight seemed compared to when he was on earth, and how his own body remained intact, stable, even in this dark cave.  

He stared at the moonlight, his expression unchanged. His gaze remained fixed.

To me, the bread seems more like a block of butter than traditional bread. It has a flavor reminiscent of wheat or milk. Crumbling bread into butter-like pieces breaks up the cheese and smooths out any surface lumps.

Still, I prefer not to eat bread shaped like the example shown. For me, it's far more satisfying—filled with crispy, buttery fragments on top, crunchy edges on the bottom, and layered buttery textures throughout. I don’t feel like I need to adjust my eating habits for this, but if you enjoy that style, we’ll need a wide variety of buttery bread crumbles.

The migration behaviors of Arctic sea urchins have remained poorly understood. As Arctic ice melted, changes such as rising salinity, ocean acidification, and increasing temperatures by 2100—along with growing carbon emissions—were observed. This new research reveals that despite greater variability in Arctic freshwater levels, both Arctic birds and sea urchins maintained their migratory routines, which are not fully reflected in current datasets.  

"Our findings demonstrate that we’ve achieved high-resolution mapping of Arctic sea urchin migratory habitats in the mid-western U.S. [Northwest] and have analyzed their migratory paths, the geographic spread from Greenland to western regions, and their movement toward the North Carolina coast," said Dr. Robert Heger from the University of Illinois at Chicago. "While migratory behavior has long been unknown, this is the first time a group of Arctic sea urchins has shown a consistent, well-defined pattern, offering a clear advancement in our understanding."  

Dr. Heger, an associate professor of sociology at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst, and M. I. Chumley from M.I.T.S. contributed to organizing the study.  

(Note: The original paper was published on November 23, 2014 (www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S008073261530033 ).)
